## Summary

Sueppel signal-boosts **Baele & Bekaert, "Stock Market Cycles" (SSRN 7649303, 2026)** — matched via Crossref exact-title search. From the quoted abstract: a **new methodology to identify bear and bull markets** in the US stock market that relies on calibrating **a single bandwidth parameter around each trading day** to define peaks and troughs; it **focuses on mean regimes** (price level, not variance) and uses **cumulated returns** [abstract truncated at capture].

The four figure panels (OCR-annotated event studies around identified crash episodes):

- **Panel A — 1987 Crash:** Sep–Dec 1987; annotations incl. "crash", Oct 1987, "Tax threatens takeovers", liquidity pledge, Hong Kong crash spillover, dollar to new lows.
- **Panel B — TMT/Dot-Com, 2000–01:** Mar–Sep 2001; NASDAQ margin-call spiral, NASDAQ 2,000, failed holiday-season rally, dot-com bankruptcies, 9/11 market reopen.
- **Panel C — GFC, 2007–09:** TARP vote, Nov 2009, Mar 6 (2009 bottom) among the recovered annotations.
- **Panel D — COVID, 2020:** 24 Feb (Italy), 09 Mar (market-wide circuit breaker), 16 Mar, 23 Mar, oil-price collapse, Fed intervention.

## Why it matters

- Regime identification is upstream of every regime-conditional idea in the vault — the same curator's [[2026-10-28-sueppel-regimerank-regime-aware-sector-ranking]] *consumes* a regime definition like this one as an input. A cleaner bull/bear segmentation (one bandwidth parameter, mean-focused, no arbitrary drawdown thresholds) would change what "regime" even means in those pipelines.
- Baele/Bekaert lineage is serious (their bull/bear and volatility-regime work is two decades deep) — this is a methods paper by people who have run these screens before, not an anonymous card.
- The event-study panels double as a compact crash-annotation atlas (1987 → COVID) — useful reference for how each historical episode actually unfolded day-by-day.
- **Skepticism gates:** SSRN working paper (2026), not yet journal-refereed; SSRN itself is Cloudflare-walled from this host, so only the abstract fragment Sueppel quoted + the four figures were captured — the "cumulated returns…" continuation and all calibration results are unread. Bandwidth-parameter methods still embed researcher choices (window, smoothing) — "one parameter" ≠ zero degrees of freedom. US-only sample.
- Reference only — no task; if the paper ever matters for a build, pull it via an authenticated session (Inbox precedent for gated papers).
